archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower from the pocket who almost never runs. Nearly all of his value comes on throws 10+ yards downfield and over the middle, not from the quick game or his legs.

report.headline: Volume up, efficiency down: Love lives downfield and dies when the pocket collapses
report.take:
Jordan Love is putting up big counting numbers, and they flatter the season a little. He's averaging 283.8 passing yards a game, second in the league, and 58.4 more per game than last year. His efficiency has gone the other way. His 0.128 EPA per dropback ranks 17th of 55, and his CPOE is down 3.4 points from last season's 5.5. Last year's 0.287 EPA per play ranked 5th. This year he's a good starter carrying a heavier load, not the top-five passer he was in 2025.

The load is the story. Green Bay's run game is last in the league at -0.187 EPA per carry, and team success rate ranks 29th. That leaves Love facing long third downs, averaging 8 yards to go, and converting only 37.6%. He has answered with the deep and intermediate game. His throws of 10+ air yards produce 0.506 EPA per attempt and 66.3 EPA in total. Everything under 10 yards nets just 3.1, and screens and swing passes behind the line have cost 11.3. Christian Watson is the vertical engine at 0.489 EPA per target. Matthew Golden gets the volume, with 102 targets at a more modest 0.199.

The totals hide how much the line decides his games. Under center, which in this offense mostly means play-action looks off a believable run threat, he has been outstanding: 0.364 EPA per play and a 15.7 CPOE. From shotgun, which is most of his dropbacks, he drops to 0.054. In the two games against Minnesota's top-ranked defense he was pressured on 47.8% and 40% of dropbacks, took 4 and 8 sacks, and produced negative EPA both times. His pressure-to-sack rate of 27.5% sits well above the 14.4% and 20.8% of the last two seasons. He's getting the ball out faster, at 2.58 seconds versus 2.89 last year, yet still absorbing sacks. That points to protection, not holding the ball.

The arc is still encouraging. Weeks 8 and 9 were the best two-game stretch of his season: a 25.6 CPOE and 18 EPA at New England. Over his last three games he's at 0.234 EPA per dropback and a 12.3 CPOE. The Minnesota dud sits inside that same window. With a clean pocket he is close to his 2025 self. Against a defense that gets home, he hasn't found an answer yet.

strengths.title: Winning at 10-plus air yards
strengths.body: Almost all of his passing value comes on throws past the sticks. Intermediate and deep attempts both return around half a point of EPA each, and he's positive in CPOE at both depths. That is the same downfield skill that drove his 2024 and 2025 seasons, so it's sustainable. Watson's 0.489 EPA per target shows he has a receiver who converts those shots.

strengths.title: Lethal from under center
strengths.body: On 70 under-center dropbacks he's at 0.364 EPA with a 15.7 CPOE and no interceptions. That's the LaFleur play-action design doing what it should: defenders bite on the run look, and he hits throws on schedule. The sample is modest. It also says the offense should lean into it more, even though the run game itself is last in the league.

strengths.title: Accuracy rebounding lately
strengths.body: A rough start, with negative CPOE in each of the first three games, dragged his season accuracy below last year's. Over the last three games he's at a 12.3 CPOE and 9.07 yards per attempt. That looks much more like the 2025 version, which ranked 8th in CPOE, than like an early-season blip.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: His pressure-to-sack rate of 27.5% is well above the last two seasons, even with a quicker release. The line allows a hit on 17.3% of dropbacks, 26th in the league. Against a defense that can get home, as in both Minnesota games, the offense stalls completely. This one is mostly protection and therefore fixable. It's also getting worse in the short term with injuries up front.

concerns.title: Short game and run game give nothing
concerns.body: Throws under 10 air yards add almost no EPA, and throws behind the line are clearly negative with a -9.6 CPOE. That means screens aren't creating easy yards. Paired with the league's worst rushing offense, every drive needs a downfield completion. That raises his weekly variance and pushes up his volume. This is a team problem, not a Love flaw, and it isn't going away with Josh Jacobs out.

concerns.title: Sloppier ball placement this year
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate is up 3 points from last year to 15.5%, 31st of 45. He's also at -0.305 EPA on 36 snaps in close fourth quarters. The late-game number is a small sample, and two of those games came in losses. The bad-throw jump is real enough to watch, but his recent accuracy suggests it's easing.

trend.note: A slow, inaccurate September gave way to two excellent games in Weeks 8-9, then he got buried by Minnesota's pass rush in Week 10. His good games are very good, and his bad ones track pressure almost exactly.

nextGame.headline: Rams take away the deep ball but rarely touch the quarterback
nextGame.body:
The Rams defense ranks 4th in pass EPA allowed. It's 3rd against deep throws at -0.215 EPA and 5th against short ones, which squeezes the exact area where Love makes his money. It allows only 219.3 passing yards a game, 4th-fewest, and holds WR1s 3.2 PPR points under their averages. The opening is up front. The Rams hit the quarterback on just 12.1% of dropbacks, 30th, and sit 18th in sack rate. Love's bad games have been pressure games, so a rush that doesn't get home gives him a real chance to play from the clean pocket where he's been sharp. Opponents have also thrown to backs more than usual against L.A., and Green Bay's backs have contributed little in the passing game.

Availability cuts both ways. Myles Garrett didn't practice Monday and is questionable, while Kobie Turner was a full participant coming off IR. The Rams' weak hit-rate numbers may partly reflect missing those two, so Garrett's status matters most for Love's afternoon. Safety Kam Curl, a 93%-snap starter, is questionable with a toe injury, and his absence would loosen the deep middle. On Green Bay's side, guard Sean Rhyan is out and tackle Travis Glover is questionable. Both are full-time starters on a line that already allows too many hits. Josh Jacobs is out, and the Rams rank 2nd against the run, so this game rests on Love's arm. The Rams are without Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and two interior linemen, which points toward a tight, lower-scoring game in line with the 43.5 total. That's an indoor setting where Green Bay probably won't be forced into catch-up volume.

keyMatchups.title: Downfield shots vs top deep defense
keyMatchups.body: Love's season is built on throws of 10+ air yards, and the Rams allow some of the least value in the league on deep balls. Expect fewer chunk plays than usual unless Curl sits. Look for Green Bay to use under-center play-action to manufacture those throws.

keyMatchups.title: Weak rush vs depleted line
keyMatchups.body: The Rams rarely hit quarterbacks, and Love has been efficient whenever he stays clean. With Rhyan out, Glover questionable and Garrett a game-time question, the trench injury report decides whether this resembles Weeks 8-9 or the Minnesota games.

keyMatchups.title: No run game to lean on
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay's run game is last in EPA per carry and faces the league's 2nd-best run defense without Jacobs. Love will likely carry a full passing load again. That supports his yardage floor but invites long-yardage downs.

nextGame.watch: How often he's sacked or hit early. If Garrett plays and the patched line leaks, the Minnesota script repeats. If the pocket holds, he can still find the intermediate middle.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume looks sustainable. A last-ranked run game and a top-10 pass rate over expected keep the ball in his hands, so a range of roughly 245 to 290 passing yards a game is reasonable, a little under his current pace as tougher pass defenses arrive. The efficiency should drift back toward his 2024-25 level rather than stay at the season mark. The recent accuracy surge, the under-center production and the long track record of downfield success all point up. His 1.9% interception rate is in line with his history, and his red-zone TD output, 13 scores despite negative EPA there, is more likely to cool slightly than climb.

The swing is protection. His pressure-to-sack rate is the clear outlier against his career, and it lines up with an injury-dented line. If Rhyan and Glover return healthy, expect sacks near 2 a game and his yards per attempt to stay around 8. If not, games like the two Minnesota losses will keep recurring against good fronts, and his weekly range will stay wide.
swingFactors: Watson staying on the field as the deep target
Any revival of the run game when Jacobs returns

confidence.note: Ten starts in a stable role with a clear career baseline, but game-to-game swings are large and line injuries are in flux.
